threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when the bus driver doesn't say 'please' or 'thank you' after you've boarded. Locals just nod and find a seat.
Caught a glimpse of a fox rummaging through someone's takeaway bag on the 333. Only in Brixton do the late-night snacks attract wildlife.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I found out my favorite Kebab shop also sells homemade baklava. It's like the hidden gems here just keep on coming.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find spontaneous parties in the park, where a DJ sets up in the middle of the afternoon with a crowd of dancing neighbors.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they navigate BART delays like they're dodging pigeons—no panic, just a resigned laugh and a quick pivot to tacos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus that rolled up to a crowd of folks, but the driver just nodded and sped off—classic Tenderloin. Some didn't even flinch.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the parks and bars, but it’s the small, old shops and their owners that keep the real charm alive.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their overly enthusiastic attempts to order 'café con leche' without a hint of an accent—it’s charming but cringy.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the buses run on time. The only thing more unreliable than them is the weather forecast!
Last night on the 59, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with an off-key rendition of ‘Wonderwall’—everyone pretended to ignore him, but we were all chuckling.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a stray cat curled up on the windowsill, soaking in the sun like it owned the place. That's when it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find spontaneous techno parties in the middle of the street after a BVG strike. It's like our own version of street carnaval.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they instinctively know to walk around the BART delays and find shortcuts through alleys you wouldn’t normally notice.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today that had a guy in a full suit trying to do a juggling act with coffee and a phone, while it stopped every two blocks. Classic San Francisco chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all fancy bar terraces; they miss the old ladies arguing over who's got the best pilates class in the park.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new if they still think La Fira de Gràcia is just a one-day event; locals know it’s a month-long street party.
